The White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913 was enacted to prohibit the manufacture, sale and use of matches made with white phosphorus. 2. The subject "white phosphorus industry" is enumerated in the Union li st of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. The White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913 is a pre-constitutional Act and no amendment has been carried out in this act since its enactment. 3. During examination of all the pre-constitutional Acts from the purview of their suitability and relevance in the present circumstances and to take remedial actions for their repeal or re -enactment or consolidation of two or more central acts into single enactment regulating identical matters for re-enactment or repeal, as the case may be, it has been decided to repeal the White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913 by the White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition (Repeal) Bill, 2025 (Annexure-I of this Note) and to save the actions taken thereunder till the appointed date. As an alternate, a notification to prohibit the usage of white phosphorus, as envisaged under the said Act shall be issued on repeal of the Act by Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to ensure that there is no regulatory gap arising on account of repeal of the Act. 4. In view of the above, comments/suggestions from the General public, Industry associations and other persons and entities concerned or being affected, is invited on the above mentioned proposed repealment. It is requested that comments/suggestion on the above stated repealment may be sent on or before 25.11.2025 in MS Office Word file to Email: pritam.k@gov.in and expl-dipp@nic.in with the subject line "Comments/suggestions on the proposed Repeal of the White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913 (5 of 1913)". -- 3 of 6 -- 5. Further, alternatively comments/suggestion may also be sent by post to th e following address: Shri Pritam Kumar Under Secretary (Explosives Section) Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Udyog Bhawan , Rafi Ahmed Kidwai Marg , Rajpath , Road Area, Central Secretariat, New Delhi- 110011 The envelope may kindly be superscripted on the top with "Comments/suggestions on the proposed Repeal of the White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913 (5 of 1913)". ~\f/ (Pritam Kumar) Under Secretary to the Govt. of India Tel: 011-23063148 Email ID: pritam.k@gov.in -- 4 of 6 -- Repeal and savings. THE WHITE PHOSPHORUS MATCHES PROHIBITION (REPEAL) BILL, 2025 A BILL to repeal the White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913. BE it enacted by Parliament in the Seventy-sixth Year o1 the Republic of India as follows : - ANNEXURE -1 1. (1) This Act may be called the White PhosphorusShort title and Matches Prohibition (Repeal) Act , 2025. commencement. (2) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint. 2. (1) With effect from such date as the Central Government may appoint in this behalf, the White Phosphorus Matches Prohibition Act, 1913 shall stand repealed : Provided that such repeal shall not effect, - (i) the orders and notifications made or issued or anything duly done or suffered under enactments under repeal till the date of their expiry , if any; or (ii) any right, privilege, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred under enactment or orders under repeal; or (iii) any penalty, forfeiture or punishment incurred in respect of any offences committed against enactment under repeal; or (iv) any investigation or remedy in respect of any penalty, forfeiture or punishment and any investigation, legal proceedings or remedy instituted, continued or enforced before the appointed date shall be continued and remain in force as if the same has instituted , continued or enforced under this Act. 5 of 1913. -- 5 of 6 -- (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no court shall take cognizance of an offence under the repealed enactment after the expiry of a period of three years from the appointed date. (3) Notwithstanding the repeal of the aforesaid enactments, the rules made under such enactment, which are in force on the date of commencement of this Act, shall continue to be in force till new rules are made under this Act. -- 6 of 6 --
